name: Mailtrap
summary: Mailtrap sells an email sending service with an API and SMTP, alongside its email testing product. The free plan covers 4,000 emails a month, Basic starts at $15 for 10,000, and Business from $85 includes a dedicated IP and 15 days of logs.

facts.text: Mailtrap's sending overview describes an Email Sending API that uses authenticated HTTP requests and SDKs, and an SMTP option for existing email clients and libraries.
Each email has its own event history, and logged events include Soft bounce, Bounce, Delivery, Open, Click, Unsubscribe, Spam, Suspension and Reject.
Log retention is 3 days on Free, 5 days on Basic, 15 days on Business and 30 days on Enterprise.
Mailtrap names SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3 and ISO 27001:2022 on its security page, and says it participates in the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 150 emails a day, 1 user, 1 domain, 3 days of logs

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: $20 for 50,000 and $30 for 100,000. 5 days of logs, no dedicated IP

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: $200 for 250,000, $300 for 500,000 and $450 for 750,000. 15 days of logs, dedicated IP included

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: $1,250 for 2,500,000 and custom pricing above. 30 days of logs

hiddenCosts: The comparison table lists extra-email rates of $1, $0.88 and $0.55 per 1,000 without labeling the plans, and overages are capped.
The page states no single sign-on option for the sending plans.

contract.cancellation: A paid plan can be cancelled at any time through the website, by phone or by email. Refunds are available within 30 days of first purchase, not for renewals.
contract.dataExport: Access ends on cancellation and user content may be deleted, though backups may persist. A deletion request can be made when cancelling.
